examples.knowledge_point: Determining the Dimensions of the Transpose of a Matrix
examples.problem:
Consider the matrix
    ${B} = 
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        1 & 2 & 4 & 2\
        4 & 4 & 1 & 1\
        3 & -3 & 0 & -1
    }
    \right\rbrack.$
What are the dimensions of ${B}^T?$
examples.worked_solution:
When a matrix is transposed, its dimensions switch from $N \times M$ to $M \times N.$

So, since $B$ is a $3 \times 4$ matrix, the transpose ${B}^T$ is a $4\times3$ matrix.

feedback.problem:
If
    $R=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 11\end{aligned}]$,
then find the transpose of $R.$

  

| ${R}^{T}=$ |  | {{field-1}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-2}} |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the transpose, we interchange the rows and columns:

$$
{R}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 11\end{aligned}]
$$
